title: 01 — Field work
tagline: What the supervisor does on site: organize the walk, capture, log and verify issues, pin them on plans, mark up photos, run checklists, read measuring tools.
intro: What the supervisor does on site: organize the walk, capture, log and verify issues, pin them on plans, mark up photos, run checklists, read measuring tools.
These are feature specifications. They describe intended behavior; use the source tree to check what is implemented today and the matching feature guide for implementation steps.

blocks.html:
• Offline-first: save work on the iPhone before relying on a network. Example: a room note stays saved in airplane mode.
  • Hash: a fixed-size fingerprint of file bytes. Example: SHA-256 can show whether a saved video changed.
  • BLE: Bluetooth Low Energy, a short-range connection used by measuring tools. Example: read a laser meter measurement nearby.
  • Glossary note: AVAssetWriter writes video to a file; jetsam is iOS stopping an app that uses too much memory; RSSI is a rough Bluetooth signal-strength reading.

Goal: build the Project → Session → Location tree faster than paper, fully offline, one-handed.

InOut
CRUD for all three; 3-level tree (floor → unit → room)Multi-user sharing (v2)
Bulk generation from a template; cloning a tree from another projectExcel/CAD import
Closing and reopening sessions
Project list → [+] New project → Project detail: [Sessions] [Locations] [Plans]
  → [+] Start session → Survey screen: locations + capture/issue badges
      → Select location → Capture (02) / Checklist (13) / Plan (11)
  → [End session] → state = closed

blocks.html:
• Modules: Packages/PlatformKit/Sources/PlatformKit/Camera, Packages/DataLayer/Sources/DataLayer/DataSources/Local/FileStorage

Goal: one AVCaptureSession for photo, video and audio without teardown; every file hashed before it reaches the DB.

InOut
Photo, video + audio, standalone audio; torch, zoom, flip, timerPhoto editing
Continuous capture with a thumbnail stripPhoto library import
GPS, deviceModel, capturedAt, trustedTime; SHA-256 on close
30-second pre-record buffer

02.1 Session and state

AVCaptureSession
├── inputs:  video (back/front), audio (mic)
├── outputs: AVCapturePhotoOutput → photos
│            AVCaptureVideoDataOutput / AudioDataOutput → AVAssetWriter
└── preview: AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer (UIViewRepresentable)

idle → configuring → ready → capturingPhoto → ready
                       ↓                        ↑
                   recording → finalizing (finishWriting + hash)
  • AVAssetWriter over AVCaptureMovieFileOutput: needed for the pre-record buffer and bitrate control over 3G.
  • startRunning/config on sessionQueue; buffers on videoDataQueue/audioDataQueue; hashing on hashQueue; UI on @MainActor. Never startRunning() on main (300–800 ms block).
  • interrupted (call, backgrounding) while recording finalizes rather than discards.

02.2 Metadata and hashing

FieldSourceWhen unavailable
capturedAtDate() at didFinishProcessingPhotoAlways present
trustedTimeClock + uptime + cached server offset (12.4)Degrades to .deviceOnly
GPS + accuracyCLLocationManager, .nearestTenMetersnil; a fix older than locationStaleAfter is nil, never wrong
sha256Streamed from the closed fileAlways present
swift
import CryptoKit
import Foundation

func sha256(ofFileAt url: URL) throws -> String {
    let handle = try FileHandle(forReadingFrom: url)
    var hasher = SHA256()

    while let chunk = try handle.read(upToCount: HashConstants.streamingChunkBytes),
          !chunk.isEmpty
    {
        hasher.update(data: chunk)
    }

    try handle.close()
    let digest = hasher.finalize()
    return digest.map { String(format: "%02x", $0) }.joined()
}

HashConstants.streamingChunkBytes is declared in the same feature module. The function propagates read and close errors to its caller; the repository boundary logs the failure.

  • Stream in chunks: Data(contentsOf:) on a 1.5 GB video triggers jetsam.
  • Files: media/<project>/<session>/<capture>.<ext>, .completeUnlessOpen, excluded from backup.

02.3 Pre-record buffer

  • Keeps the last 30 s when record is pressed.
  • Never raw buffers in RAM: AVAssetWriter writes 3-second segments to <Caches>/prebuffer/ in a ring of segmentCount; on record, join with AVMutableComposition.
  • Off by default; disables below minBatteryLevel.
swift
enum CaptureConstants {
    static let videoBitrate: Int = 8_000_000
    static let maxVideoDuration: TimeInterval = 600
    static let locationStaleAfter: TimeInterval = 120
    static let minFreeDiskBytesForVideo: Int64 = 500 * 1024 * 1024
}
enum PreRecordConstants {
    static let segmentDuration: TimeInterval = 3
    static let segmentCount: Int = 10
    static let minBatteryLevel: Float = 0.20
}
enum HashConstants { static let streamingChunkBytes: Int = 1_048_576 }
RiskHandling
Disk fills mid-recordingCheck free space first; below threshold, block video and state the remainder
Thermal throttling.serious → lower bitrate; .critical → stop deliberately
PermissionsCamera, mic, location handled separately, never one combined alert
RotationPreview and writer transforms must match, or video is rotated in the PDF

Done

  • 50 photos with flat memory
  • 3-minute 1080p plays back and hash reproduces
  • Call mid-recording finalizes to .pending
  • Airplane mode + denied location still captures

Tests

  • Hash against known vectors and shasum on 200 MB
  • State machine rejects recording during photo
  • Interruption finalizes once
  • Stale GPS → nil
  • Ring buffer eviction. All run without a camera via CaptureSessionControlling

• Modules: SiteLog/Presentation/Issues, DomainLayer, DataLayer

  • Core business feature: prove "broken last week, fixed now" with two photos of the same spot.

Goal: log an issue in under 20 s, one-handed; in a later session reopen it at the same location, shoot verification, render the pair in the PDF.

InOut
Issue CRUD, multiple captures, severity, status, due dateAccount-linked assignment (subcontractors have no app)
Assignee and trade (free text, autocompleted)Multi-user comment threads (v2)
Carry-over of open issues; pairing and closure by verification photo
Phrase library, on-device dictation, voice notes

03.1 Flows

Log:     Capture → shoot → [Attach issue] → sheet (description, severity=Major,
         assignee, due, 🎤 dictate · 🔊 voice note · 📍 pin) → Save → back to camera
Verify:  New session → location → banner "3 open issues from 12 Aug" → issue
         → [Shoot verification] with prior photo at 30% overlay → [Resolved] [Still open] [Worse]
Close:   new Issue (status .verified, verification photo); old.resolvedByIssue = new,
         old.status = .resolved; original captures never touched
DecisionReason
Sheet returns to the cameraThe user is walking a room; each camera restart costs ~1 s
Default severity .majorDefaulting to minor makes everything minor
assigneeName is free textA name that groups the PDF is what gets used on site
30% overlayWithout it the angles differ and the pair is worthless
  • Phrase library: ~30 seeded phrases; new typed phrases added; sorted by usage; synced via the backend's phrases table.

03.2 Design

swift
struct IssuePairing: Sendable, Equatable {
    let previous: IssueSnapshot
    let current: IssueSnapshot?
    let outcome: PairingOutcome   // .resolved / .stillOpen / .worsened
}

enum IssueDefaults {
    static let severity: IssueSeverity = .major
    static let dueDateOffsetDays: Int = 7
    static let maxCapturesPerIssue: Int = 20
    static let overlayOpacity: Double = 0.30
    static let staleIssueSessionThreshold: Int = 3
}
  • PairIssuesUseCase lives in DomainLayer, imports no frameworks — the most error-prone logic in the app.
  • Upload priority: critical 100 · major 50 · minor 10 · no issue 5 · video −20 (video blocks dozens of photos behind it).
RiskHandling
Location deleted or renamed between sessionsDelete blocked while open issues exist; rename keeps id + audit entry
Verification at the wrong spotOverlay; the PDF prints Location.code under every image
Issues piling upPast staleIssueSessionThreshold the banner changes color and the PDF gets a section

Done

  • One issue with photo in under 20 s, measured
  • Session 2 surfaces exactly the 3 open issues offline
  • Closing leaves the original byte-identical

Tests

  • Pairing with 0/1/n open issues
  • Skips .verified
  • Closing never mutates prior captures
  • Priority across severity × kind
  • Delete-with-open-issues rejected
  • Phrase ordering tie-break

blocks.html:
• Module: Packages/PlatformKit/Sources/PlatformKit/Bluetooth · mock: Tools/MockPeripheral/

Goal: scan → connect → read a laser distance or moisture meter (Bosch GLM, Leica Disto) → attach the reading to a Capture.

  • BLE for control and small values; files never go over BLE.
swift
public protocol DeviceProfile: Sendable {
    static var serviceUUID: CBUUID { get }
    static var notifyCharacteristicUUID: CBUUID { get }
    static func parse(_ data: Data) throws -> DeviceReading   // pure, tested on captured bytes
}

public struct DeviceReading: Sendable, Codable, Equatable {
    public let value: Double
    public let unit: MeasurementUnit      // .meter / .millimeter / .percentMoisture
    public let kind: MeasurementKind      // .distance / .area / .moisture
    public let measuredAt: Date
    public let deviceName: String
}
  • One file per vendor profile. Named DeviceReading because Foundation.Measurement collides.
  • poweredOff → poweredOn → scanning → connecting → discovering → ready; disconnected is normal (meters sleep). DeviceLinkManager is an actor.
  • CoreBluetooth rules: keep a strong CBPeripheral reference, no commands before .poweredOn, check errors on both discover callbacks, reconnect via retrievePeripherals(withIdentifiers:).
  • UX: reading overlays the preview; status is a colored dot, no alerts; never blocks capture. Readings older than measurementStaleAfter are not attached.
  • The macOS mock scripts invalid values, disconnects and garbage bytes, and makes CI possible.
swift
enum DeviceLinkConstants {
    static let scanTimeout: TimeInterval = 15
    static let connectTimeout: TimeInterval = 10
    static let reconnectBaseDelay: TimeInterval = 2
    static let reconnectMaxDelay: TimeInterval = 60
    static let minimumRSSI: Int = -85
    static let measurementStaleAfter: TimeInterval = 30
    static let backgroundDisconnectDelay: TimeInterval = 300
}

Risks

  • No hardware for byte formats → start on the mock and ship a raw-bytes "generic" profile
  • Permission denied → feature hides itself
  • Battery → no background scanning

Done

  • Reads from the mock into a capture
  • Killing the mock greys the dot, capture still works
  • Relaunch reconnects within 10 s

Tests

  • Vendor parse on real bytes
  • Truncated/bad-checksum payloads throw
  • Unit conversion
  • Stale reading not attached
  • Reconnect backoff capped
  • Full flow against the mock

• Modules: Packages/PlatformKit/Sources/PlatformKit/Rendering (tiles), Packages/DataLayer/Sources/DataLayer/DataSources/Local/FileStorage (plan files), SiteLog/Presentation/Plans

Goal: import a floor plan, pin issues at exact coordinates, print a pin map per sheet.

  • Out: DWG/CAD, measuring, plan editing.
swift
import SwiftData

@Model
final class PlanSheetModel {
    var id: UUID
    var project: ProjectModel
    var name: String
    var sourceFileURL: URL
    var pageIndex: Int
    var pixelSize: CGSize
    var sha256: String
    var location: LocationModel?
}

@Model
final class PlanPinModel {
    var id: UUID
    var sheet: PlanSheetModel
    var issue: IssueModel
    var normalizedPoint: NormalizedPoint
    var createdAt: Date
}
  • Coordinates are 0…1, never pixels, so pins survive re-rendering at any scale. CGPoint only inside Plans.
  • One pin per issue; every move writes an audit entry.
  • Rendering: CATiledLayer tiles on demand (A0 at 300 dpi never becomes one bitmap), PDFKit or CGImageSource as source, tile cache in <Caches>/plans/, pins in an overlay view.
  • Interaction: long-press drops a pin (tap is for panning), tap opens the issue, drag confirms on release. Pins colored by severity, hollow when resolved, clustered below clusterZoomThreshold.
  • Import: Files or share sheet; multi-page PDFs choose pages (one PlanSheet each); hashed; uploaded at low priority; capped at maxPlanFileBytes.
swift
enum PlanConstants {
    static let maxPlanFileBytes: Int64 = 100 * 1024 * 1024
    static let maxZoomScale: CGFloat = 8
    static let clusterZoomThreshold: CGFloat = 2
    static let clusterRadiusPoints: CGFloat = 24
    static let pinDropLongPressDuration: TimeInterval = 0.4
    static let tileSize: CGSize = CGSize(width: 512, height: 512)
    static let uploadPriority: Int = 1
}
RiskHandling
Revised drawingNew PlanSheet, offer to migrate pins by normalized coordinate, keep the old sheet
Encrypted or corrupt PDFRejected at import with the reason
Pin on the wrong sheetSheet name at the viewer top and under every pin map

Done

  • 20-page A1 PDF, 50 pins, 60 fps pan/zoom
  • A0 peak memory under 150 MB
  • Pins land on the same spot after relaunch at a different zoom
  • Fully offline

Tests

  • planPoint round-trip through zoom/pan
  • Same point at two scales
  • Clustering
  • Oversized and encrypted imports rejected
  • Pin migration
  • Sheet delete blocked while pins exist
  • A0 memory

blocks.html:
• Modules: Packages/PlatformKit/Sources/PlatformKit/Rendering (stamped copies), DomainLayer (models)

Rule: the original file is never touched; markup is a separate layer; stamps are a derived copy.

12.1 Annotation layer

swift
struct NormalizedPoint: Codable, Sendable, Equatable { var x: Double; var y: Double }
struct NormalizedRect:  Codable, Sendable, Equatable { var origin: NormalizedPoint; var width: Double; var height: Double }

enum AnnotationShape: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    case arrow(from: NormalizedPoint, to: NormalizedPoint, style: AnnotationStyle)
    case rect(NormalizedRect, style: AnnotationStyle)
    case ellipse(NormalizedRect, style: AnnotationStyle)
    case freehand(points: [NormalizedPoint], style: AnnotationStyle)
    case text(String, at: NormalizedPoint, style: AnnotationTextStyle)
}
  • Annotation { id, capture, shapes: [AnnotationShape] (JSON), createdAt, updatedAt }, 1:1 with a capture. Normalized so phone markup renders correctly on A4. Normalized* exist because DomainLayer may not import CoreGraphics; AnnotationStyle avoids clashing with SwiftUI.ShapeStyle.
  • Keeps the hash valid, stays editable, prints annotated or clean, syncs as a few KB.
  • Editor: Arrow (default), Box, Circle, Pen, Text; stroke scales with image size; undo capped at maxUndoSteps; commits on exit. Edits write an audit entry.

12.2 Stamped derivatives

  • File: derived/<…>/<captureID>-stamped.jpg.
  • Carries date/time, coordinates and accuracy, project, location code, logo.
  • Generated on demand, cached; never hashed, never evidence, excluded from integrity checks.

12.3 Dictation and voice notes

  • SFSpeechRecognizer, requiresOnDeviceRecognition = true: site audio never leaves the device.
  • Vietnamese and English; falls back to the phrase library.
  • A voice note is an ordinary audio Capture; dictated text lands in Issue.detail.

12.4 Trusted time

swift
struct TrustedTimestamp: Codable, Sendable {
    let deviceTime: Date
    let uptimeNanos: UInt64         // detects clock jumps within a launch
    let serverOffset: TimeInterval? // serverTime − deviceTime
    let offsetMeasuredAt: Date?
    let confidence: TimeConfidence
}
ConfidenceCondition
.serverVerifiedOffset measured within serverOffsetValidity, under maxAcceptableOffset
.sessionConsistentNo server contact, uptime matches wall-clock progression
.deviceOnlyClock jumped, or relaunched with no server contact

• Modules: SiteLog/Presentation/Checklists, DomainLayer, DataLayer

Goal: walk a location against a template, tick items, turn a failed item into an issue without retyping.

  • Out: weighted scoring, branching, regulatory libraries.
swift
import SwiftData

@Model
final class ChecklistTemplateModel {
    var id: UUID
    var name: String
    var appliesTo: LocationKind?
    var items: [ChecklistTemplateItemModel]
    var isBuiltIn: Bool
    var usageCount: Int
}

@Model
final class ChecklistTemplateItemModel {
    var id: UUID
    var order: Int
    var text: String
    var defaultSeverity: IssueSeverity
    var requiresPhotoOnFail: Bool
}

@Model
final class ChecklistRunModel {
    var id: UUID
    var template: ChecklistTemplateModel
    var session: SessionModel
    var location: LocationModel
    var startedAt: Date
    var completedAt: Date?
    var results: [ChecklistResultModel]
}

@Model
final class ChecklistResultModel {
    var id: UUID
    var templateItem: ChecklistTemplateItemModel
    var outcome: ChecklistOutcome
    var note: String
    var issue: IssueModel?
    var answeredAt: Date?
}
  • A run stores its own results; editing a template never rewrites completed runs.
  • Flow: pick a template (recent first) → one row per item [✓ Pass] [✕ Fail] [– N/A] → fail opens the camera if required and prefills the issue sheet (03) → header progress "14/22"; finish at 100% answered. One tap per item in the common case; runs are resumable.
  • Built-ins (handover: living room, bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, balcony; electrical; plumbing; structural) are editable and duplicable, not deletable; edits fork a copy. Templates export/import as JSON.
  • The PDF gets a per-location table (item, outcome, note, issue) — it shows what passed too.
swift
enum ChecklistConstants {
    static let maxItemsPerTemplate: Int = 200
    static let recentTemplateCount: Int = 5
    static let templateExportVersion: Int = 1
}

Risks

  • Tick-through without inspecting is visible from per-answer timestamps
  • Imported JSON is validated (version, item cap) and treated as data

Done

  • 22-item run offline, two fails → two prefilled issues
  • Kill mid-run resumes
  • Template edit leaves the completed run and its PDF section unchanged

Tests

  • Fail creates one issue with item text and severity
  • Fail → pass resolves it
  • Template edit does not alter runs
  • Completion percentage
  • JSON import validation
  • Built-ins fork on edit
